assignments.reason: Truth (אמת) is identified in Torah #9 as the essential quality that draws God's presence, which in turn enables prayer. The Rebbe says 'הקדוש ברוך הוא הוא עצם האמת' — God IS truth itself. In this Torah, אמת functions as the spiritual counterpart of אמונה (faith), which is already in Package 1. Both are faces of the same reality: genuine spiritual orientation toward God that enables and empowers prayer. Its nature is the inner quality of authentic devotion, not a separate domain.
The ability to pray is, by its very definition, a dimension of prayer itself. It describes prayer's accessibility or capacity — the state of being ready/able to pray. Its essential nature is prayer.

assignments.node_id: הוא מאיר לו איך ליצא מהחשך המונע אותו בתפלתו
assignments.reason: Divine illumination that enables one to exit the darkness obstructing prayer. Its essential nature is the breakthrough into prayer — it describes the prayer-enabling moment when God lights the way through the klipot. This is the experiential dynamic of prayer overcoming its obstacles, squarely within the prayer domain.

assignments.node_id: הוא מתקן "תחתים שנים ושלישים", הינו עולם השפל ועולם הגלגלים ועולם השכל
assignments.reason: The repair of the three worlds (lower, celestial, intellectual) is the cosmic effect of proper prayer. While 'tikkun' could be its own domain, in Torah #9 this concept appears exclusively as what prayer accomplishes — it is the cosmic reach of תפלה. Its essential nature in THIS Torah is the scope/power of prayer, not an independent cosmological concept.

assignments.node_id: הקדוש־ברוך־הוא חומד מלמעלה לשכן עם האדם
assignments.reason: God's desire to dwell with the person is the divine response to truthful prayer. In Torah #9, this is not an abstract theological concept — it is the mechanism by which prayer works: truth draws God's presence, which illuminates the way through darkness to proper prayer. Its nature is the divine dimension of the prayer dynamic.

God dwelling with the person — the actualized divine presence — is the spiritual state that enables prayer to function. In Torah #9, this is the bridge between truth and illumination: truth causes God's presence, which causes the light that opens the way through darkness. This is internal to the prayer-faith-truth cluster of Package 1.

Vitality/life-force is identified in the very first line of the teaching: 'עקר החיות מקבלין מהתפלה' — the essence of vitality is received from prayer. In this Torah, חיות is not a general concept but is explicitly equated with what prayer provides. It is the essential product of prayer, making it part of the prayer domain in Torah #9.

Finding the opening (in the darkness) is the experience of breaking through to prayer. The 'petach' (opening) in Torah #9 section ג is the escape from the klipot that surround the person during prayer. Its essential nature is the breakthrough moment of prayer itself.

Seeing that one's words emerge truthfully from one's mouth — this describes the quality of authentic prayer-speech. Its essential nature is truthful prayer, the fusion of אמת and תפלה that is the core mechanism of Torah #9 section ג. This is the experiential description of what proper prayer looks like.

God yearning from above to dwell near you — functionally identical to 'הקדוש ברוך הוא חומד מלמעלה לשכן עם האדם'. This is the divine response within the prayer dynamic, the mechanism by which truth enables prayer. Part of the prayer/faith/truth cluster of Package 1.

When God dwells with you, He illuminates for you — this is the illumination stage of the prayer dynamic. The Rebbe's chain: truth -> God's presence -> illumination -> finding the opening -> prayer. This node describes the light that enables prayer to break through the surrounding darkness. It is inherently about the prayer mechanism.

assignments.node_id: מתפלל בכל כחו ומכניס כחו באותיות התפלה
assignments.reason: Praying with all one's strength and investing one's power in the letters of prayer — this IS prayer at its most intense. The essential nature is the act of wholehearted prayer itself, the opening teaching of Torah #9 section א.

His strength is renewed there — the renewal that occurs through investing oneself fully in prayer. The Rebbe links this to 'חדשים לבקרים רבה אמונתך' — renewal is tied to אמונה=תפלה. The nature of this concept in Torah #9 is the regenerative power of prayer.

The word that emerges in truth — this is the unit of truthful prayer-speech (the Rebbe interprets 'תבה' as both 'word' and 'ark'). Its essential nature is the spoken prayer word uttered with sincerity. This belongs to the prayer domain.

assignments.node_id: תשים לך פתח בחשך שאתה נצוד בו
assignments.reason: The truthful word opens a doorway in the darkness that traps you — this is the breakthrough of prayer through the klipot. The 'darkness' is the prayer-obstacle (מחשבות זרות וקליפות of section ג), and the 'opening' is the prayer-breakthrough. Its nature is the liberation of prayer from obstruction.

Sustaining one's Father in heaven through prayer — this concept describes what prayer accomplishes in the heavenly realm. While it involves 'sustenance' (פרנסה), the essential nature here is the prayer-function: it is the person's PRAYER that does the sustaining. The concept is about prayer's cosmic role, not about livelihood. Compare with 'ויעמידה ליעקב לחק' where עמידה=תפלה and חק=מזונא — prayer IS the sustenance of heaven.

The union of God and Shekhinah is the cosmic/heavenly zivvug. Package 5 is the domain of מטה — זווג ופרנסה (union and sustenance). While this union is CAUSED by prayer, its essential nature is divine union (זווג), not prayer itself. The Rebbe explicitly frames it: 'בני ישראל בתפלתם גורמים זווגא דקודשא בריך הוא ושכינתה' — prayer causes the union, but the union itself is a distinct reality. Package 5 already contains זווג as one of its core nodes.

The heavenly union caused through prayer — this describes the mechanism of causing zivvug. While it mentions תפלה as the cause, the concept itself describes the union-dimension. Its essential nature is the zivvug domain: how much union one produces. Package 5 is the zivvug/parnasa domain.

Meriting one's marital match — this is the earthly zivvug, the personal union one receives. The Rebbe says 'לפי הזווג שגורם בתפלתו כן זוכה לזווגו' — prayer causes heavenly union which causes earthly union. The essential nature of this node is personal union/marriage, squarely in the זווג domain of Package 5.

Livelihood/sustenance — Package 5 already contains ממון (money/wealth) as a bechina of מטה. פרנסה (sustenance) is the same domain: the earthly reward dimension of prayer. The Rebbe states 'כפי שמפרנס לאביו שבשמים בתפלתו כן נותנין לו פרנסתו' — one's sustenance corresponds to one's prayer, but פרנסה itself is about livelihood, not prayer.

Binding one's prayer to the tzaddik of the generation — this describes the person's relationship to the tzaddik. While it involves 'prayer', the essential concept is the tzaddik-connection: section ד opens with 'צריך כל אדם לקשר את תפלתו לצדיק הדור'. The nature of this node is the role and function of the tzaddik, which is Package 3's domain.

assignments.node_id: להעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך
assignments.reason: Elevating each prayer to its proper gate — this is the tzaddik's unique spiritual function. The Rebbe says 'והצדיק יודע לכוין השערים ולהעלות כל תפלה ותפלה לשער השיך'. This is what defines the tzaddik in Torah #9: his ability to route prayers. The essential nature is the tzaddik's role, not prayer itself.

new_packages.label: לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה
new_packages.reason: לומד תורה (learning Torah) appears as a cause-node enabling prayer ('אי אפשר להתפלל רק כשלומד תורה'). Its essential nature is Torah study — a distinct spiritual domain from prayer, faith, the tzaddik, or union/sustenance. No existing package covers this domain. While it is only one node from the eitza edges, Torah study is a fundamental spiritual category in Rebbe Nachman's teachings, and in Torah #9 it is explicitly identified as the prerequisite without which prayer cannot exist. The teaching cites 'לא עם הארץ חסיד' and 'מסיר אזנו משמע תורה גם תפלתו תועבה' to establish Torah study as its own independent domain.
